response.title: Power station or computer battery backup for a reef tank: which one switches over by itself and lasts longer?
response.answer:
For a reef tank, a power station with built-in UPS functionality is usually the best choice if you want both automatic switchover and long battery life.

The important distinction is that not every power station switches over automatically, whereas almost every computer UPS does.

Power station vs. computer UPS

Feature

	

Power station

	

Computer UPS




Automatic switchover

	

Only models with UPS/EPS functionality

	

Yes




Switchover speed

	

Typically 10–30 ms, model dependent

	

Typically 2–10 ms




Battery runtime

	

Usually much longer

	

Usually shorter




Battery technology

	

Often LiFePO4

	

Often lead-acid




Battery lifespan

	

Often 2,000–4,000+ cycles

	

Often 3–5 years of service




Best use

	

Extended outages

	

Short outages and sensitive electronics

My recommendation for a reef tank: Get a LiFePO4 power station that supports automatic switchover, and plug your return pump and circulation pumps into it.

You generally don't need to keep your reef lights running during an outage. Water circulation and oxygenation are more important.

How long will it run your reef tank?

Assuming a power station has 85% usable capacity after inverter losses, here are estimated runtimes:

Actual runtimes can be shorter, particularly with low loads and inverter standby consumption. For comparison, an APC BR1500G computer UPS is rated for approximately 73 minutes at 100 W.

For a reef tank, **a power station with built-in UPS functionality is usually the best choice** if you want both automatic switchover and long battery life.

The important distinction is that **not every power station switches over automatically**, whereas almost every computer UPS does.

## Power station vs. computer UPS

| Feature | Power station | Computer UPS |
|---|---|---|
| Automatic switchover | Only models with UPS/EPS functionality | Yes |
| Switchover speed | Typically 10–30 ms, model dependent | Typically 2–10 ms |
| Battery runtime | Usually much longer | Usually shorter |
| Battery technology | Often LiFePO4 | Often lead-acid |
| Battery lifespan | Often 2,000–4,000+ cycles | Often 3–5 years of service |
| Best use | Extended outages | Short outages and sensitive electronics |

**My recommendation for a reef tank:** Get a LiFePO4 power station that supports automatic switchover, and plug your return pump and circulation pumps into it.

You generally don't need to keep your reef lights running during an outage. Water circulation and oxygenation are more important.

## How long will it run your reef tank?

Assuming a power station has 85% usable capacity after inverter losses, here are estimated runtimes:

| Equipment running | 500 Wh station | 1,000 Wh station | 2,000 Wh station |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 20 W circulation pump | 21 hours | 42 hours | 85 hours |
| 50 W pumps | 8.5 hours | 17 hours | 34 hours |
| 100 W pumps + equipment | 4.3 hours | 8.5 hours | 17 hours |
| 200 W including heater | 2.1 hours | 4.3 hours | 8.5 hours |

Actual runtimes can be shorter, particularly with low loads and inverter standby consumption. For comparison, an APC BR1500G computer UPS is rated for approximately 73 minutes at 100 W. <Cite ref="turn501505search25"/>
